---
title: "Analysis of Viromes"
author: "Aydin Karatas"
output: html_document
---


This report compares virome features among paleofecal/coprolite (`pal`),
modern non-industrial (`pre`), and modern industrial (`ind`) samples. It
summarizes phage lifestyle, functional diversity, virulence-factor signals,
and SourceTracker-estimated source contributions. Unless stated otherwise,
group summaries use bootstrap medians and comparisons use Kruskal–Wallis
tests.

## Analysis setup
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
base_dir <- "~/Documents/ucla/research/project_coprolite_viromes/analysis/"
knitr::opts_chunk$set(root.dir = base_dir)

# load the analysis helpers from the statistics, graphing, and miscellaneous
# directories.
library(tidyverse)
source_files_from_dir <- function(directory) {
  full_path <- file.path(base_dir, directory)
  functions_list <- list.files(
    path = full_path,
    pattern = "*.R",
    full.names = TRUE
    )
  sapply(functions_list, source)
}
source_files_from_dir("stats")
source_files_from_dir("graphing")
source_files_from_dir("misc")

# define the shared random seed, input/output directories, and bootstrap size.
set.seed(seed = 123)
data_dir <- "~/Documents/ucla/research/project_coprolite_viromes_NOT_CODE/data/20261019"
figs_dir <- "~/Documents/ucla/research/project_coprolite_viromes_NOT_CODE/figures"
max_iter <- 1000
MIN_TOTAL_ORFS <- 5L
subset_top <- 100
# star_bounds <- list(list(0.025, 0.975), list(0.01, 0.99),
#                     list(0.001, 0.999))
star_bounds <- list(list(0.025, 0.975))
```

## Phage lifestyle predictions

Lifestyle-prediction counts are read per sample and converted to total count,
temperate-to-virulent ratios, and the fraction predicted temperate. The main
comparison uses the temperate-to-virulent ratio, with group- and
country-level bootstrap medians, a paleofecal-size downsampling sensitivity
analysis, violin plots, and Kruskal–Wallis tests.

```{r lifestyle boot}
# read lifestyle counts and remove samples excluded from this analysis.
lifestyle_counts <- read.csv(
  file = paste0(data_dir, "/lifestyle_counts.csv"),
  header = TRUE,
  row.names = 1
  )
lifestyle_counts <- lifestyle_counts %>% select(
  -pal.AUT_2612, -pal.ENG_LG4560.69, -pal.BEL_SRS510175
  )
# derive total counts, the unadjusted ratio, a +1 pseudocount ratio for
# zero-safe comparison, and the temperate fraction.
lifestyle_counts["total", ] <- colSums(lifestyle_counts)
lifestyle_counts["temp_to_lyt", ] <- 
  lifestyle_counts["temperate", ] / lifestyle_counts["virulent", ]
lifestyle_counts["temp_to_lyt_+1", ] <- 
  (lifestyle_counts["temperate", ] + 1) / (lifestyle_counts["virulent", ] + 1)
lifestyle_counts["temp_perc", ] <-
  lifestyle_counts["temperate", ] / lifestyle_counts["total", ]
lifestyle_counts <- t(lifestyle_counts)
# retain samples with more than 100 lifestyle predictions before summarizing.
lifestyle_counts <- lifestyle_counts[lifestyle_counts[, "total"] > 100, ]
lifestyle_counts <- t(lifestyle_counts)
lifestyle_counts_t <- as.data.frame(t(lifestyle_counts))
lifestyle_counts_t$group <- sub("\\..*$", "", rownames(lifestyle_counts_t))
lifestyle_counts_t$country <- sub("^[^.]+\\.([A-Za-z]{3}).*$", "\\1", rownames(lifestyle_counts_t))

# bootstrap group and country medians of the temperate-to-virulent ratio.
lifestyle_boot_res <- get_row_median(
  data = lifestyle_counts,
  num_iter = max_iter, 
  row_num = 5,
  cats = c("ind", "pre", "pal")
  )
lifestyle_median_by_country <- get_row_median(
  data = lifestyle_counts,
  num_iter = max_iter, 
  row_num = 5,
  cats = c("AUT", "AWC", "BMS", "ZAF", "ZAP",
           "CHN", "DNK", "ESP", "USA",
           "FJI", "MEX", "MDG", "TZA", "NPL", "PER"), 
  bootstrap = FALSE
  )
lifestyle_median_by_country_sep_pal <- get_row_median(
  data = lifestyle_counts,
  num_iter = max_iter, 
  row_num = 5,
  cats = c("pal.AUT_2604", "pal.AUT_2610", "pal.AUT_2611", "pal.AWC_AW107", "pal.AWC_AW108", "pal.AWC_AW110A", "pal.BMS_UT30.3",
           "pal.BMS_UT43.2", "pal.ZAF_SRS4491529", "pal.ZAP_Zape1", "pal.ZAP_Zape2", "pal.ZAP_Zape3" ,
           "CHN", "DNK", "ESP", "USA",
           "FJI", "MEX", "MDG", "TZA", "NPL", "PER"), 
  bootstrap = FALSE
  )
lifestyle_boot_res_by_country <- get_row_median(
  data = lifestyle_counts,
  num_iter = max_iter, 
  row_num = 5,
  cats = c("AUT", "AWC", "BMS", "ZAF", "ZAP",
           "CHN", "DNK", "ESP", "USA",
           "FJI", "MEX", "MDG", "TZA", "NPL", "PER"), 
  bootstrap = TRUE
  )
pal_size <- nrow(lifestyle_counts_t %>% filter(group == "pal"))
# downsample each group to the number of paleofecal samples for a balanced
# comparison.
lifestyle_boot_res_downsample <- get_row_median(
  data = lifestyle_counts,
  num_iter = max_iter, 
  row_num = 5,
  cats = c("ind", "pre", "pal"),
  max_resample = pal_size
  )

# produce group, country, and balanced-group violin plots with bootstrap
# intervals.
lifestyle_voilin <- create_cat_voilins(
  data = lifestyle_boot_res, 
  ci_offset = c(0.15, 0.55, 0.55),
  file_name = "lifestyle",
  plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/lifestyle"),
  cats_order = c("pal", "pre", "ind"),
  plot.title = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio",
  x.title = "Sample group",
  y.title = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio"
  )
lifestyle_voilin[[1]]
lifestyle_voilin[[2]]
lifestyle_voilin_by_country <- create_cat_voilins(
  data = lifestyle_boot_res_by_country, 
  ci_offset = 0.3,
  file_name = "lifestyle_by_country",
  plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/lifestyle"),
  cats_order = c("AUT", "AWC", "BMS", "ZAF", "ZAP",
                 "FJI", "MDG", "MEX", "NPL", "PER", "TZA",
                 "CHN", "DNK", "ESP", "USA"),
  plot.title = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio",
  x.title = "Sample origin",
  y.title = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio"
  )
lifestyle_voilin_by_country[[1]]
lifestyle_voilin_by_country[[2]]
lifestyle_voilin_downsampled <- create_cat_voilins(
  data = lifestyle_boot_res_downsample, 
  ci_offset = c(0.15, 0.55, 0.55),
  file_name = "lifestyle_downsampled",
  plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/lifestyle"),
  cats_order = c("pal", "pre", "ind"),
  plot.title = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio",
  x.title = "Sample group",
  y.title = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio"
  )
lifestyle_voilin_downsampled[[1]]
lifestyle_voilin_downsampled[[2]]

# test whether bootstrap ratio distributions differ among groups and countries.
lifestyle <- reshape2::melt(lifestyle_boot_res)
kruskal.test(lifestyle$value, lifestyle$Var2)
lifestyle_by_country <- reshape2::melt(lifestyle_boot_res_by_country)
kruskal.test(lifestyle_by_country$value, lifestyle_by_country$Var2)
lifestyle_downsampled <- reshape2::melt(lifestyle_boot_res_downsample)
kruskal.test(lifestyle_downsampled$value, lifestyle_downsampled$Var2)
```

### Paleofecal samples and country summaries

This supplementary figure displays individual paleofecal observations as
points and bootstrap distributions for the modern-country groups as violins;
diamonds mark medians and intervals summarize the bootstrap distributions.

```{r supplemetary lifestyle plot}
# use bootstrap draws for modern-country violins and raw values for the
# paleofecal-country points.

boot_wide <- lifestyle_boot_res_by_country
raw_df <- lifestyle_counts_t[, c("country", "temp_to_lyt")]
colnames(raw_df) <- c("cat", "value")
violin_cats <- c("FJI","MDG","MEX","NPL","PER","TZA","CHN","DNK","ESP","USA")
dot_cats    <- c("AUT","AWC","BMS","ZAF","ZAP")

cats_order <- c("AUT","AWC","BMS","ZAF","ZAP","FJI","MDG","MEX","NPL","PER","TZA","CHN","DNK","ESP","USA")

# convert both inputs to a common long format and retain their display groups.
boot_long <- reshape2::melt(as.data.frame(boot_wide)) %>%
  setNames(c("cat", "value")) %>%
  mutate(
    value = as.numeric(value),
    source = "boot"
  ) %>%
  filter(cat %in% violin_cats)

raw_long <- raw_df %>%
  transmute(
    cat = as.character(cat),
    value = as.numeric(value),
    source = "raw"
  ) %>%
  filter(cat %in% dot_cats)

plot_df <- bind_rows(boot_long, raw_long) %>%
  mutate(cat = factor(cat, levels = cats_order))

# calculate 95% bootstrap intervals for the violin groups only.
ci_data <- plot_df %>%
  filter(source == "boot") %>%
  group_by(cat) %>%
  summarise(
    median_value = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    ymin = quantile(value, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    ymax = quantile(value, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    x_pos = as.numeric(cat),
    # offset interval bars slightly so they remain visible beside each violin.
    x_lab_pos = x_pos + 0.15
  )

first_mid    <- (ci_data$ymin[1] + ci_data$ymax[1]) / 2
first_x_text <- ci_data$x_lab_pos[1] + 0.1

# define the shared grayscale and interval colors used in this supplementary
# figure.
grey_border <- brewer.pal(9, "Greys")[8]
grey_fill   <- brewer.pal(9, "Greys")[2]
ci_color    <- brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")[10]


# draw individual paleofecal points, modern bootstrap violins, medians, and
# their uncertainty intervals.
p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = cat)) +
  # draw raw points only for the paleofecal-country groups.
  geom_point(
    data = subset(plot_df, source == "raw"),
    aes(y = value), pch = 21, fill = grey_fill, 
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0),
    size = 5.5, alpha = 0.9,
    color = ci_color, stroke = 1
  ) +
  # draw violin distributions only for the bootstrap-based modern groups.
  geom_violin(
    data = subset(plot_df, source == "boot"),
    aes(y = value, fill = cat), 
    color = grey_border, linewidth = 1, trim = TRUE, width = 1
  ) +
  # use a consistent gray fill across violin groups.
  scale_fill_manual(values = rep(grey_fill, length(cats_order)), guide = "none") +
  # mark each displayed group's median with a diamond.
  stat_summary(
    aes(y = value),
    fun = median, geom = "point",
    fill = grey_border, color = grey_fill, stroke = 1,
    pch = 23, size = 5.5
  ) +
  # add intervals only where bootstrap draws provide uncertainty estimates.
  geom_segment(
    data = ci_data,
    aes(x = x_lab_pos, xend = x_lab_pos, y = ymin, yend = ymax),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 2, color = ci_color
  ) +
  # annotate(
  #   "text", x = first_x_text, y = first_mid,
  #   label = "95% CI", angle = -90, size = 8, color = ci_color
  # ) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio",
    x = "Sample origin",
    y = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(20, 5, 20, 20, "points"),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 14, color = "black", face = "bold", hjust = -0.5),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 12, color = "black", face = "bold", angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_line(linewidth = 2, color = "black"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", size = 2, fill = NA)
  )

p

ggsave(
  file.path(paste0(figs_dir, "/lifestyle"), "lifestyle_by_country_pal_dots.svg"), p, 
  height = 7, width = 9
  )
```

## Bacterial ORF functional diversity on phage contigs

Raw counts of bacterial enzyme-commission (EC) annotations on predicted
phage contigs provide the input for a Shannon-diversity analysis. The analysis
excludes the listed samples, calculates per-sample diversity, and produces a
raw-diversity plot plus bootstrap-median violin plots by sample group.

```{r metabolic gene analysis: read data}
# read EC-annotation counts and remove samples excluded from this analysis.
vir_ec_counts <- read.csv(
  file = paste0(data_dir, "/bac_on_phage_ec_counts.csv"),
  header = TRUE,
  row.names = 1
  ) 
vir_ec_counts <- vir_ec_counts %>% select(
  -pal.ENG_LG4560.69_annotation_bac, -pal.AUT_2612_annotation_bac
  )
```

```{r metabolic gene analysis: diversity}
# calculate Shannon diversity per sample and bootstrap its group medians.
diversity_data <- get_diversity_indeces(
  data = t(vir_ec_counts),
  div_index = "shannon",
  num_iter = max_iter
)

# plot the unaggregated per-sample Shannon diversity values.
diversity_plot <- create_diversity_plots(
  data = diversity_data[[1]],
  div_index = "Shannon", 
  file_name = "shannon_raw",
  plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/diversity")
  )
diversity_plot

# plot the bootstrapped group medians and their uncertainty intervals.
diversity_violin <- create_cat_voilins(
  data = diversity_data[[2]], 
  ci_offset = c(0.2, 0.55, 0.55),
  file_name = "shannon_medians",
  plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/diversity"), 
  cats_order = c("pal", "pre", "ind"),
  plot.title = "Shannon diversity of bacterial ORFs on predicted phage contigs",
  x.title = "Sample group",
  y.title = "Shannon diversity")
diversity_violin[[1]]
diversity_violin[[2]]
```

## Virulence-factor representation across groups

The following analyses use Virulence Factor Database (VFDB) annotations to
measure the prevalence and contig coverage of qualifying hits, assess a
selected network-contig subset, and identify differentially represented VFDB
entries and categories.

### Reference preparation

VFDB metadata are reshaped into the identifier and category fields needed to
annotate subsequent hit-count results.

```{r vfdb alignment: format reference}
# read VFDB metadata and retain the identifier, name, and category fields.
vf_meta_data <- read.csv(
  file = paste0(data_dir, "/VFs.csv"),
  header = TRUE)
vf_reference <- vf_meta_data
colnames(vf_reference) <- vf_reference[1, ]
vf_reference <- vf_reference[-1, c("VFID", "VFCID", "VF_Name", "VFcategory")]
```

### Single-set full-pool VFDB analysis

This analysis uses one independently regenerated inventory and pooled
sample summary, using the unsuffixed set B inputs below. These bacterial-mode
calls are on predicted phage contigs; hits are sequence-similarity signals.
Annotation status does not restrict the search pool. Outputs are written
under the selected version's figure directory.

```{r versioned contig VFDB analysis, results='asis'}
# use regenerated set B tables and validate their provenance.
vfdb.input.paths <- file.path(data_dir, c(
  phage.stats = "phage_vf_stats.csv",
  sample.stats = "sample_vf_stats.csv",
  orfs = "phage_vf_orfs.csv"
))
names(vfdb.input.paths) <- c("phage.stats", "sample.stats", "orfs")
vfdb.version <- "VFDB_setB"
vfdb.label <- sub("VFDB_set", "VFDB set ", vfdb.version)

# analyze the selected reference set once.
run.contig.vf.analysis <- function(vfdb.version, vfdb.input.paths,
                                   figs_dir) {
  cat("### Phage-level lifestyle and VFDB statistics\n\nThe unit in these descriptive comparisons is one predicted phage contig,\nwhich is not necessarily a complete phage genome. Both statistics use the\nsame qualifying set of VFDB hits from all bacterial-mode Prokka CDS calls\nafter the full-sequence\nE-value, score, and bias thresholds have been applied. Unknown lifestyle\nclassifications remain in the source table but are excluded from these\ntwo-level plots.", "\n\n")
  # read and validate one threshold-consistent row per predicted phage contig.
  phage.columns <- c(
    "category", "origin", "sample", "contig_id", "lifestyle",
    "contig_length", "total_bacterial_orfs", "qualifying_vf_orfs",
    "vf_orf_prevalence", "vf_covered_bases", "vf_contig_coverage",
    "orf_pool", "vfdb_version"
  )
  phage.vf.stats <- data.table::fread(
    vfdb.input.paths[["phage.stats"]], select = phage.columns,
    data.table = FALSE
  )
  validate.vf.pool(phage.vf.stats, vfdb.version)
  phage.vf.plot.data <- prepare.phage.vf.plot.data(phage.vf.stats) %>%
    select(category, origin, lifestyle, vf.orf.prevalence, vf.contig.coverage)
  sample.vf.coverage <- pool.phage.vf.coverage(
    data = phage.vf.stats,
    exclusions = c("pal.ENG_LG4560.69", "pal.BEL_SRS510175")
  )
  rm(phage.vf.stats)
  invisible(gc())

  # compare qualifying VFDB-hit ORF prevalence by lifestyle across sample groups.
  phage.vf.prevalence.group.plot <- create.phage.vf.plot(
    data = phage.vf.plot.data,
    statistic = "vf.orf.prevalence",
    facet.variable = "category",
    plot.title = "Phage-level VFDB-hit ORF prevalence by sample group",
    y.title = "Qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs / all Prokka ORFs"
  )
  print(phage.vf.prevalence.group.plot)
  ggsave(
    filename = paste0(
      figs_dir, "/vf/phage_vf_orf_prevalence_by_group.svg"
    ),
    plot = phage.vf.prevalence.group.plot,
    height = 7,
    width = 9
  )

  # compare qualifying VFDB-hit ORF prevalence by lifestyle across origins.
  phage.vf.prevalence.origin.plot <- create.phage.vf.plot(
    data = phage.vf.plot.data,
    statistic = "vf.orf.prevalence",
    facet.variable = "origin",
    plot.title = "Phage-level VFDB-hit ORF prevalence by sample origin",
    y.title = "Qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs / all Prokka ORFs"
  )
  print(phage.vf.prevalence.origin.plot)
  ggsave(
    filename = paste0(
      figs_dir, "/vf/phage_vf_orf_prevalence_by_origin.svg"
    ),
    plot = phage.vf.prevalence.origin.plot,
    height = 10,
    width = 14
  )

  # compare qualifying VFDB-hit ORF coverage by lifestyle across sample groups.
  phage.vf.coverage.group.plot <- create.phage.vf.plot(
    data = phage.vf.plot.data,
    statistic = "vf.contig.coverage",
    facet.variable = "category",
    plot.title = "Phage-level VFDB-hit contig coverage by sample group",
    y.title = "Fraction of phage-contig bases covered"
  )
  print(phage.vf.coverage.group.plot)
  ggsave(
    filename = paste0(
      figs_dir, "/vf/phage_vf_contig_coverage_by_group.svg"
    ),
    plot = phage.vf.coverage.group.plot,
    height = 7,
    width = 9
  )

  # compare qualifying VFDB-hit ORF coverage by lifestyle across origins.
  phage.vf.coverage.origin.plot <- create.phage.vf.plot(
    data = phage.vf.plot.data,
    statistic = "vf.contig.coverage",
    facet.variable = "origin",
    plot.title = "Phage-level VFDB-hit contig coverage by sample origin",
    y.title = "Fraction of phage-contig bases covered"
  )
  print(phage.vf.coverage.origin.plot)
  ggsave(
    filename = paste0(
      figs_dir, "/vf/phage_vf_contig_coverage_by_origin.svg"
    ),
    plot = phage.vf.coverage.origin.plot,
    height = 10,
    width = 14
  )
  # release full-data plot inputs once all four SVGs have been written.
  rm(phage.vf.plot.data, phage.vf.prevalence.group.plot,
     phage.vf.prevalence.origin.plot, phage.vf.coverage.group.plot,
     phage.vf.coverage.origin.plot)
  invisible(gc())
  cat("### Per-ORF prevalence\n\nAll bacterial-mode Prokka proteins are searched, including hypothetical\nand named non-EC proteins. Alignments are filtered with stringent\nE-value, score, and bias thresholds. For each sample and ORF, only the\nbest-ranked qualifying hit is retained, then counts are completed with zeros\nfor samples lacking a hit.", "\n\n")
  # filter to qualifying VFDB alignments and retain the dominant hit per
  # sample--ORF pair before tabulating counts.
  sample.vf.stats <- read.csv(
    vfdb.input.paths[["sample.stats"]]
  )
  validate.vf.pool(sample.vf.stats, vfdb.version)
  if (anyDuplicated(sample.vf.stats$sample)) {
    stop("Duplicate sample VFDB summaries")
  }
  sample.vf.stats <- sample.vf.stats %>%
    filter(!sample %in% c("pal.ENG_LG4560.69", "pal.AUT_2612"))
  vf.counts.long <- read.vf.inventory.counts(
    vfdb.input.paths[["orfs"]], vfdb.version, sample.vf.stats$sample
  )
  write.csv(sample.vf.stats, file.path(figs_dir, "sample_vf_stats.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  vf_counts <- vf.counts.long %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
    rename(VFID = vf_id)
  rm(vf.counts.long)

  all_samples <- sample.vf.stats$sample
  missing_samples <- setdiff(all_samples, colnames(vf_counts))

  for (sample_name in missing_samples) {
    vf_counts[[sample_name]] <- 0
  }

  vf_counts <- tibble(
    VFID = union(as.character(vf_reference$VFID), vf_counts$VFID)
  ) %>% left_join(vf_counts, by = "VFID")
  vf_counts[is.na(vf_counts)] <- 0

  vf_counts <- vf_counts %>%
    select(VFID, all_of(all_samples)) %>%
    column_to_rownames("VFID")
  cat("The prevalence denominator includes all bacterial-mode Prokka calls on\npredicted phage contigs. Samples with totals greater than `MIN_TOTAL_ORFS`\n(default 5) are retained. Sample prevalence uses pooled ORF counts, with\npositive-denominator zero-hit samples retained as zero. Bootstrap group and\ncountry summaries, balanced downsampling, and Kruskal\u2013Wallis tests are retained.", "\n\n")
  # use pooled sample totals for prevalence and sample eligibility.
  vf_prot_counts <- sample.vf.stats %>%
    filter(total_bacterial_orfs > MIN_TOTAL_ORFS) %>%
    transmute(sample, vfdb_count = qualifying_vf_orfs,
              total = total_bacterial_orfs, proportion = vf_orf_prevalence)
  vf_prot_counts <- vf_prot_counts %>%
    select(sample, vfdb_count, total, proportion) %>%
    pivot_longer(-sample, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = value)
  vf_prot_counts_t <- as.data.frame(t(vf_prot_counts))
  vf_prot_counts_t$group <- sub("\\..*$", "", rownames(vf_prot_counts_t))
  vf_prot_counts_t$country <- sub("^[^.]+\\.([A-Za-z]{3}).*$", "\\1", rownames(vf_prot_counts_t))
  colnames(vf_prot_counts_t) <- c(vf_prot_counts_t[1, ][1:3], "group", "country")
  vf_prot_counts_t <- vf_prot_counts_t[-1, ]
  vf_prot_counts_t$vfdb_count <- as.numeric(vf_prot_counts_t$vfdb_count)
  vf_prot_counts_t$total <- as.numeric(vf_prot_counts_t$total)
  vf_prot_counts_t$proportion <- as.numeric(vf_prot_counts_t$proportion)

  # compare eligible samples' lifestyle ratios with their VFDB-hit ORF
  # prevalence. Each sample must pass both the lifestyle total (>100) and
  # total bacterial ORFs (>MIN_TOTAL_ORFS) eligibility filters used above.
  lifestyle_vf_plot_data <- lifestyle_counts_t %>%
    rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
    transmute(
      sample = sample,
      temp_to_lyt = as.numeric(temp_to_lyt),
      group = factor(group, levels = c("pal", "pre", "ind")),
      country = factor(
        sub("^[^.]+\\.([A-Za-z]{3}).*$", "\\1", sample),
        levels = c(
          "AUT", "AWC", "BMS", "ZAF", "ZAP", "FJI", "MDG", "MEX",
          "NPL", "PER", "TZA", "CHN", "DNK", "ESP", "USA"
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    inner_join(
      vf_prot_counts_t %>%
        rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
        transmute(
          sample = sample,
          vf_orf_prevalence = as.numeric(proportion)
        ),
      by = "sample"
    ) %>%
    filter(is.finite(temp_to_lyt), is.finite(vf_orf_prevalence))

  if (anyDuplicated(lifestyle_vf_plot_data$sample) > 0 ||
      !identical(
        sort(unique(as.character(lifestyle_vf_plot_data$group))),
        c("ind", "pal", "pre")
      ) ||
      any(!is.finite(lifestyle_vf_plot_data$temp_to_lyt)) ||
      any(!is.finite(lifestyle_vf_plot_data$vf_orf_prevalence))) {
    stop("Lifestyle-VFDB plot data must contain one finite row per sample and ",
         "all sample groups.")
  }

  lifestyle_vf_plot <- ggplot(
    lifestyle_vf_plot_data,
    aes(x = temp_to_lyt, y = vf_orf_prevalence)
    ) +
    geom_point(
      shape = 21,
      fill = "grey70",
      color = "black",
      alpha = 0.55,
      size = 2
    ) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(
      vars(group),
      scales = "fixed",
      labeller = as_labeller(c(
        pal = "Paleofecal/coprolite",
        pre = "Modern non-industrial",
        ind = "Modern industrial"
      ))
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio and VFDB-hit ORF prevalence",
      x = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio",
      y = "Qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs / all Prokka ORFs"
    ) +
    theme_bw()
  print(lifestyle_vf_plot)

  ggsave(
    filename = paste0(
      figs_dir,
      "/lifestyle/lifestyle_vf_orf_prevalence.svg"
    ),
    plot = lifestyle_vf_plot,
    height = 7,
    width = 7
  )

  lifestyle_vf_country_plot <- lifestyle_vf_plot +
    facet_wrap(vars(country), scales = "fixed")
  print(lifestyle_vf_country_plot)

  ggsave(
    filename = paste0(
      figs_dir,
      "/lifestyle/lifestyle_vf_orf_prevalence_by_country.svg"
    ),
    plot = lifestyle_vf_country_plot,
    height = 10,
    width = 14
  )

  # bootstrap medians of qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs per bacterial-mode Prokka ORF.
  vf_prot_boot_res <- get_row_median(
    data = vf_prot_counts,
    num_iter = max_iter,
    row_num = 3,
    cats = c("ind", "pre", "pal")
    )
  vf_prot_boot_res_by_country <- get_row_median(
    data = vf_prot_counts,
    num_iter = max_iter,
    row_num = 3,
    cats = c("AUT", "AWC", "BMS", "ZAF", "ZAP",
             "CHN", "DNK", "ESP", "USA",
             "FJI", "MEX", "MDG", "TZA", "NPL", "PER")
    )
  pal_size_vf_prot <- nrow(vf_prot_counts_t %>% filter(group == "pal"))
  # balance the bootstrap resampling size to the paleofecal group.
  pal_size_vf_prot_boot_res_downsample <- get_row_median(
    data = vf_prot_counts,
    num_iter = max_iter,
    row_num = 3,
    cats = c("ind", "pre", "pal"),
    max_resample = pal_size_vf_prot
    )

  # produce group, country, and balanced-group prevalence violin plots.
  vf_prot_voilin <- create_cat_voilins(
    data = vf_prot_boot_res,
    ci_offset = c(0.15, 0.55, 0.55),
    file_name = "vf_perc",
    plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/vf"),
    cats_order = c("pal", "pre", "ind"),
    plot.title = "Qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs / all Prokka ORFs",
    x.title = "Sample group",
    y.title = "Qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs / all Prokka ORFs"
    )
  print(vf_prot_voilin[[1]])
  print(vf_prot_voilin[[2]])
  vf_prot_voilin_by_country <- create_cat_voilins(
    data = vf_prot_boot_res_by_country,
    ci_offset = 0.3,
    file_name = "vf_perc_by_pop",
    plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/vf"),
    cats_order = c("AUT", "AWC", "BMS", "ZAF", "ZAP",
                   "FJI", "MDG", "MEX", "NPL", "PER", "TZA",
                   "CHN", "DNK", "ESP", "USA"),
    plot.title = "Qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs / all Prokka ORFs",
    x.title = "Sample origin",
    y.title = "Qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs / all Prokka ORFs"
    )
  print(vf_prot_voilin_by_country[[1]])
  print(vf_prot_voilin_by_country[[2]])
  vf_prot_voilin_downsampled <- create_cat_voilins(
    data = pal_size_vf_prot_boot_res_downsample,
    ci_offset = c(0.15, 0.55, 0.55),
    file_name = "vf_perc_downsampled",
    plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/vf"),
    cats_order = c("pal", "pre", "ind"),
    plot.title = "Qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs / all Prokka ORFs",
    x.title = "Sample group",
    y.title = "Qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs / all Prokka ORFs"
    )
  print(vf_prot_voilin_downsampled[[1]])
  print(vf_prot_voilin_downsampled[[2]])

  # test prevalence differences among group and country bootstrap distributions.
  vf_prot <- reshape2::melt(vf_prot_boot_res)
  print(kruskal.test(vf_prot$value, vf_prot$Var2))
  vf_prot_by_country <- reshape2::melt(vf_prot_boot_res_by_country)
  print(kruskal.test(vf_prot_by_country$value, vf_prot_by_country$Var2))
  vf_prot_downsampled <- reshape2::melt(pal_size_vf_prot_boot_res_downsample)
  print(kruskal.test(vf_prot_downsampled$value, vf_prot_downsampled$Var2))
  cat("### Contig coverage\n\nThis section measures the fraction of phage-contig bases covered by qualifying\nVFDB-hit ORFs. After removing excluded samples, it summarizes coverage with\nbootstrap medians, country-level and downsampled comparisons, violin plots,\nand Kruskal\u2013Wallis tests.", "\n\n")
  # use sample coverage pooled before releasing the phage table above.

  # retain the established metric-by-sample layout for bootstrap summaries.
  vf_contig_hits <- sample.vf.coverage %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -sample,
      names_to = "metric",
      values_to = "value"
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = sample, values_from = value) %>%
    column_to_rownames("metric")
  vf_contig_hits <- vf_contig_hits[
    c(
      "sample.vf.covered.bases",
      "sample.phage.bases",
      "sample.vf.contig.coverage"
    ),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  # compare lifestyle ratios with the fraction of phage-contig bases covered by
  # qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs. Retain the same eligible samples as the ORF-
  # prevalence plot and discard non-finite coverage values.
  lifestyle_vf_coverage_plot_data <- lifestyle_vf_plot_data %>%
    select(sample, temp_to_lyt, group, country) %>%
    inner_join(
      sample.vf.coverage %>%
        transmute(
          sample = sample,
          vf_contig_coverage = sample.vf.contig.coverage
        ),
      by = "sample"
    ) %>%
    filter(is.finite(temp_to_lyt), is.finite(vf_contig_coverage))

  if (anyDuplicated(lifestyle_vf_coverage_plot_data$sample) > 0 ||
      !identical(
        sort(unique(as.character(lifestyle_vf_coverage_plot_data$group))),
        c("ind", "pal", "pre")
      ) ||
      any(!is.finite(lifestyle_vf_coverage_plot_data$temp_to_lyt)) ||
      any(!is.finite(lifestyle_vf_coverage_plot_data$vf_contig_coverage))) {
    stop("Lifestyle-VFDB coverage plot data must contain one finite row per ",
         "sample and all sample groups.")
  }

  lifestyle_vf_coverage_plot <- ggplot(
    lifestyle_vf_coverage_plot_data,
    aes(x = temp_to_lyt, y = vf_contig_coverage)
    ) +
    geom_point(
      shape = 21,
      fill = "grey70",
      color = "black",
      alpha = 0.55,
      size = 2
    ) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(
      vars(group),
      scales = "fixed",
      labeller = as_labeller(c(
        pal = "Paleofecal/coprolite",
        pre = "Modern non-industrial",
        ind = "Modern industrial"
      ))
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio and VFDB-hit contig coverage",
      x = "Temperate-to-virulent phage ratio",
      y = "Fraction of phage-contig bases covered by VFDB-hit ORFs"
    ) +
    theme_bw()
  print(lifestyle_vf_coverage_plot)

  ggsave(
    filename = paste0(
      figs_dir,
      "/lifestyle/lifestyle_vf_contig_coverage.svg"
    ),
    plot = lifestyle_vf_coverage_plot,
    height = 7,
    width = 7
  )

  lifestyle_vf_coverage_country_plot <- lifestyle_vf_coverage_plot +
    facet_wrap(vars(country), scales = "fixed")
  print(lifestyle_vf_coverage_country_plot)

  ggsave(
    filename = paste0(
      figs_dir,
      "/lifestyle/lifestyle_vf_contig_coverage_by_country.svg"
    ),
    plot = lifestyle_vf_coverage_country_plot,
    height = 10,
    width = 14
  )

  # bootstrap medians of the fraction of total phage-contig length covered by
  # qualifying VFDB-hit ORFs.
  vf_aln_boot_res <- get_row_median(
    data = vf_contig_hits,
    num_iter = max_iter,
    row_num = 3,
    cats = c("pal", "pre", "ind")
    )
  vf_aln_boot_res_by_country <- get_row_median(
    data = vf_contig_hits,
    num_iter = max_iter,
    row_num = 3,
    cats = c("AUT", "AWC", "BEL", "BMS", "ZAP", "ZAF",
             "CHN", "DNK", "ESP", "USA",
             "FJI", "MEX", "MDG", "TZA", "NPL", "PER")
    )
  pal_size_vf_prot <- nrow(vf_prot_counts_t %>% filter(group == "pal"))
  # use the paleofecal sample count as the balanced resampling size.
  pal_size_vf_aln_boot_res_downsample <- get_row_median(
    data = vf_contig_hits,
    num_iter = max_iter,
    row_num = 3,
    cats = c("ind", "pre", "pal"),
    max_resample = pal_size_vf_prot
    )

  # produce group, country, and balanced-group contig-coverage violin plots.
  vf_aln_voilin <- create_cat_voilins(
    data = vf_aln_boot_res,
    ci_offset = c(0.15, 0.55, 0.55),
    file_name = "vf_aln",
    plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/vf"),
    cats_order = c("pal", "pre", "ind"),
    plot.title = "Fraction of phage-contig bases covered by VFDB-hit ORFs",
    x.title = "Sample group",
    y.title = "Fraction of phage-contig bases covered")
  print(vf_aln_voilin[[1]])
  print(vf_aln_voilin[[2]])
  vf_aln_voilin_by_country <- create_cat_voilins(
    data = vf_aln_boot_res_by_country,
    ci_offset = c(0.15, 0.55, 0.55),
    file_name = "vf_aln_by_pop",
    plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/vf"),
    cats_order = c("AUT", "AWC", "BMS", "ZAP", "ZAF",
                   "FJI", "MDG", "MEX", "NPL", "PER", "TZA",
                   "CHN", "DNK", "ESP", "USA"),
    plot.title = "Fraction of phage-contig bases covered by VFDB-hit ORFs",
    x.title = "Sample origin",
    y.title = "Fraction of phage-contig bases covered")
  print(vf_aln_voilin_by_country[[1]])
  print(vf_aln_voilin_by_country[[2]])
  vf_aln_voilin_downsampled <- create_cat_voilins(
    data = pal_size_vf_aln_boot_res_downsample,
    ci_offset = c(0.15, 0.55, 0.55),
    file_name = "vf_aln_downsampled",
    plot_dir = paste0(figs_dir, "/vf"),
    cats_order = c("pal", "pre", "ind"),
    plot.title = "Fraction of phage-contig bases covered by VFDB-hit ORFs",
    x.title = "Sample group",
    y.title = "Fraction of phage-contig bases covered"
    )
  print(vf_aln_voilin_downsampled[[1]])
  print(vf_aln_voilin_downsampled[[2]])

  # test coverage differences among group and country bootstrap distributions.
  vf_aln <- reshape2::melt(vf_aln_boot_res)
  print(kruskal.test(vf_aln$value, vf_aln$Var2))
  vf_aln_by_country <- reshape2::melt(vf_aln_boot_res_by_country)
  print(kruskal.test(vf_aln_by_country$value, vf_aln_by_country$Var2))
  vf_aln_downsampled <- reshape2::melt(pal_size_vf_aln_boot_res_downsample)
  print(kruskal.test(vf_aln_downsampled$value, vf_aln_downsampled$Var2))
  cat("### Differential representation\n\nNormalized VFDB counts are compared among groups to rank individual VFDB\nentries by Kruskal\u2013Wallis and pairwise tests. The resulting table is joined to\nVFDB categories; category frequencies are summarized overall, among entries\nwith Kruskal\u2013Wallis *p* <= 0.05, and among the top-ranked entries for the\nsubsequent heatmap selection.", "\n\n")
  # normalize VFDB counts before comparing representation among sample groups.
  vf_norm <- normalize_data(vf_counts)
  vf_t_norm <- t(vf_norm)
  vf_t_scale <- scale(vf_t_norm)

  # rank differentially represented VFDB entries and attach their VFDB
  # categories.
  vf_diff_repres <- get_diff_repres_cols(data = vf_t_norm)
  vf_diff_repres <- cbind(rownames(vf_diff_repres), vf_diff_repres)
  colnames(vf_diff_repres) <- c("VFID", colnames(vf_diff_repres)[-1])
  vf_diff_repres <- merge(x = vf_diff_repres, y = vf_reference, by = "VFID", all.x = TRUE)
  write.csv(vf_counts, file.path(figs_dir, "vf_counts.csv"))
  write.csv(vf_diff_repres, file.path(figs_dir, "vf_diff_repres.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  vf_diff_repres$kruskal_p <- as.numeric(vf_diff_repres$kruskal_p)
  vf_diff_repres$ind_vs_pre_p <- as.numeric(vf_diff_repres$ind_vs_pre_p)
  vf_diff_repres$ind_vs_pal_p <- as.numeric(vf_diff_repres$ind_vs_pal_p)
  vf_diff_repres$pre_vs_pal_p <- as.numeric(vf_diff_repres$pre_vs_pal_p)
  vf_diff_repres <- vf_diff_repres[order(vf_diff_repres[, "kruskal_p"]), ]

  # summarize the most frequent VFDB categories across all ranked entries and
  # statistically significant entries.
  vfc_freq <- vf_diff_repres %>%
    filter(!is.na(VFCID)) %>% count(Var1 = VFCID, name = "Freq")
  vfc_freq <- as.data.frame(vfc_freq)
  vfc_freq <- merge(vfc_freq, unique(vf_meta_data[-1, c(5,6)]),
                    by.x = "Var1", by.y = "X.3")
  vfc_freq <- vfc_freq[rev(order(vfc_freq$Freq)), ]
  print(vfc_freq)

  vfc_sig_freq <- vf_diff_repres %>%
    filter(!is.na(VFCID), !is.na(kruskal_p), kruskal_p <= 0.05) %>%
    count(Var1 = VFCID, name = "Freq")
  vfc_sig_freq <- as.data.frame(vfc_sig_freq)
  vfc_sig_freq <- merge(vfc_sig_freq, unique(vf_meta_data[-1, c(5,6)]),
                        by.x = "Var1", by.y = "X.3")
  vfc_sig_freq <- vfc_sig_freq[rev(order(vfc_sig_freq$Freq)), ]
  print(vfc_sig_freq)

  vfc_subset_freq <- vf_diff_repres %>%
    slice_head(n = subset_top) %>% filter(!is.na(VFCID)) %>%
    count(Var1 = VFCID, name = "Freq")
  vfc_subset_freq <- as.data.frame(vfc_subset_freq)
  vfc_subset_freq <- merge(vfc_subset_freq, unique(vf_meta_data[-1, c(5,6)]),
                           by.x = "Var1", by.y = "X.3")
  vfc_subset_freq <- vfc_subset_freq[rev(order(vfc_subset_freq$Freq)), ]
  print(vfc_subset_freq)


  # use Jenks natural breaks on top-category frequencies to select the heatmap
  # cutoff.
  library(BAMMtools)
  vfc_break <- getJenksBreaks(var = vfc_subset_freq$Freq, k = 4)[[2]]
  vfc_colors <- which(vfc_subset_freq$Freq == vfc_break)[1]
  return(invisible(NULL))
}

version.figs.dir <- file.path(figs_dir, vfdb.version)
for (directory in c("", "vf", "lifestyle")) {
  dir.create(file.path(version.figs.dir, directory), recursive = TRUE,
             showWarnings = FALSE)
}
cat("### ", vfdb.label, "\n\n", sep = "")
run.contig.vf.analysis(vfdb.version, vfdb.input.paths, version.figs.dir)
```

## SourceTracker attribution of coprolite samples

SourceTracker provides estimated proportions and standard deviations for the
Industrial, NonIndustrial, Soil, and Unknown source categories. The figures
show proportions with plus-or-minus-one-standard-deviation intervals, a
log-scale view for small contributions, and two log-ratio summaries: modern
(Industrial + NonIndustrial) versus Soil, and Non-industrial versus
Industrial. Positive log ratios indicate that the numerator source category is
more strongly represented.

```{r plot source tracker results}
# read SourceTracker's estimated source proportions and their standard
# deviations.
mixing_props <- read.table(
  file = paste0(data_dir, "/sourcetracker_output/mixing_proportions.txt"),
  header = 1, sep = "\t")
mixing_sds <- read.table(
  file = paste0(data_dir, "/sourcetracker_output/mixing_proportions_stds.txt"),
  header = 1, sep = "\t")
mixing_props
mixing_sds
```

```{r plot mixing proportions from sourcetracker}
# create the output directory and reshape SourceTracker estimates into a
# sample-by-source table.
source.tracker.fig.dir <- paste0(figs_dir, "/sourcetracker")
dir.create(source.tracker.fig.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

get.sample.label <- function(sample.id) {
  sub("^([^_]+)_([^_]+).*", "\\1_\\2", sample.id)
}

props.long <- mixing_props %>%
  mutate(sample = get.sample.label(SampleID)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(SampleID, sample),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "prop"
  )

sds.long <- mixing_sds %>%
  mutate(sample = get.sample.label(SampleID)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(SampleID, sample),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "sd"
  )

# join proportions to their standard deviations, order source categories, and
# bound displayed uncertainty intervals to the probability scale.
source.levels <- c("Industrial", "NonIndustrial", "Soil", "Unknown")
source.labels <- c("Industrial", "Non-industrial", "Soil", "Unknown")
source.colors <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "Greys")[c(8, 6, 4, 2)]

mixing.df <- props.long %>%
  inner_join(sds.long, by = c("SampleID", "sample", "source")) %>%
  mutate(
    source = factor(source, levels = source.levels),
    sample = factor(sample, levels = unique(sample)),
    ymin = pmax(0, prop - sd),
    ymax = pmin(1, prop + sd)
  )

# plot source proportions with plus-or-minus-one-standard-deviation intervals.
dodge.width <- 0.8
mixing.prop.plot <- ggplot(
  mixing.df,
  aes(x = sample, y = prop, fill = source)
) +
  geom_col(
    color = "black",
    position = position_dodge(width = dodge.width),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
    position = position_dodge(width = dodge.width),
    width = 0.3,
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(labels = source.labels, values = source.colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "SourceTracker Mixing Proportions",
    x = "Coprolite sample",
    y = "Estimated source proportion",
    fill = "Source"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(20, 30, 30, 20, "points"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold",
                                margin = margin(r = 20)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = -30, hjust = 0, size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )

print(mixing.prop.plot)

ggsave(
  filename = paste0(source.tracker.fig.dir, "/mixing_proportions.svg"),
  plot = mixing.prop.plot,
  height = 8,
  width = 14
)

# for the log-scale plot, replace zeros and zero-bounded intervals with half
# the smallest observed nonzero proportion so they can be displayed.
min.nonzero.prop <- min(mixing.df$prop[mixing.df$prop > 0], na.rm = TRUE)
log.floor <- min.nonzero.prop / 2

mixing.log.df <- mixing.df %>%
  mutate(
    prop.log = pmax(prop, log.floor),
    ymin.log = pmax(ymin, log.floor),
    ymax.log = pmax(ymax, log.floor)
  )

mixing.log.plot <- ggplot(
  mixing.log.df,
  aes(x = sample, fill = source)
) +
  geom_col(
    aes(y = prop.log),
    color = "black",
    position = position_dodge(width = dodge.width),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = ymin.log, ymax = ymax.log),
    position = position_dodge(width = dodge.width),
    width = 0.3,
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(labels = source.labels, values = source.colors) +
  scale_y_log10(
    limits = c(1e-5, 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "SourceTracker Mixing Proportions",
    subtitle = paste0("Log10 y axis; zeros shown at ", signif(log.floor, 2)),
    x = "Coprolite sample",
    y = "Estimated source proportion (log10)",
    fill = "Source"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(20, 30, 30, 20, "points"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold",
                                margin = margin(r = 20)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = -30, hjust = 0, size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )

print(mixing.log.plot)

ggsave(
  filename = paste0(source.tracker.fig.dir, "/mixing_proportions_log10.svg"),
  plot = mixing.log.plot,
  height = 8,
  width = 14
)

# calculate log10 ratios for modern-versus-soil and non-industrial-versus-
# industrial contributions using the same zero-safe floor.
source.ratio.df <- mixing.df %>%
  select(sample, source, prop) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = prop) %>%
  mutate(
    soil.prop = pmax(Soil, log.floor),
    human.prop = pmax(Industrial + NonIndustrial, log.floor),
    industrial.prop = pmax(Industrial, log.floor),
    nonindustrial.prop = pmax(NonIndustrial, log.floor),
    human.vs.soil = log10(human.prop / soil.prop),
    nonindustrial.vs.industrial = log10(
      nonindustrial.prop / industrial.prop
    )
  ) %>%
  select(sample, human.vs.soil, nonindustrial.vs.industrial) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(human.vs.soil, nonindustrial.vs.industrial),
    names_to = "ratio",
    values_to = "log10.fold.change"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ratio = factor(
      ratio,
      levels = c("human.vs.soil", "nonindustrial.vs.industrial"),
      labels = c(
        "Modern / Soil",
        "Non-industrial / Industrial"
      )
    )
  )

source.ratio.colors <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "Greys")[c(8, 5)]

source.ratio.plot <- ggplot(
  source.ratio.df,
  aes(x = sample, y = log10.fold.change, fill = ratio)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_col(
    color = "black",
    position = position_dodge(width = dodge.width),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = source.ratio.colors) +
  labs(
    title = "SourceTracker Log Ratios",
    subtitle = paste0("Values above zero indicate numerator > denominator; ",
                      "zeros shown at ", signif(log.floor, 2)),
    x = "Coprolite sample",
    y = "log10 source ratio",
    fill = "Ratio"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(20, 30, 30, 20, "points"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold",
                                margin = margin(r = 20)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = -30, hjust = 0, size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(0.6, "cm"),
    legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )

print(source.ratio.plot)

ggsave(
  filename = paste0(source.tracker.fig.dir, "/sourcetracker_log10_ratios.svg"),
  plot = source.ratio.plot,
  height = 8,
  width = 14
)

source.ratio.summary <- source.ratio.df %>%
  mutate(
    ratio = case_when(
      ratio == "Modern / Soil" ~ "modern_vs_soil_log10",
      ratio == "Non-industrial / Industrial" ~
        "nonindustrial_vs_industrial_log10"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(sample, ratio, log10.fold.change) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = ratio,
    values_from = log10.fold.change
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample = factor(sample, levels = unique(source.ratio.df$sample))
  )

source.ratio.summary

readr::write_tsv(
  source.ratio.summary,
  file = paste0(source.tracker.fig.dir, "/source_ratio_summary.tsv")
)
```
